Increase this if one large scan should finish faster.

Higher values can noticeably increase CPU, disk, and memory usage. Adjust it carefully to match your system.

libraries.parallelScanJobsTooltip:
This controls how many libraries MediaLyze may scan at the same time.

Higher values increase overall resource usage. Keep an eye on CPU, disk, and memory pressure.
Maximum: {{max}}.
libraries.comparisonScatterPointLimitTooltip:
Caps how many points MediaLyze returns for comparison scatter plots.

Heatmaps and bar charts stay exact; only scatter plots are sampled for readability and browser performance.

Warning: very high values can noticeably increase browser memory use and make large comparison views sluggish.

historyRetention.title: History retention
historyRetention.daysTooltip:
How many days MediaLyze keeps entries for this history type before pruning older records.

0 means unlimited.
historyRetention.storageLimitTooltip:
The maximum estimated storage this history type may use before MediaLyze prunes the oldest records.

0 means unlimited.
historyRetention.scopeNote: File history retention only affects per-file snapshots; dashboard and media library trends use the separate media library history.
historyRetention.reconstructTooltip:
Builds approximate past history from the current media set and inferred add dates based mainly on file mtimes.

This can be inaccurate: mtimes are not guaranteed to match when a file was actually added, and deleted or changed files from the past cannot be reconstructed reliably.

Reconstruction only fills as much history as would still be kept by the current retention days and storage limits configured in this panel.

Missing earlier history is filled in, and older existing snapshots can be enriched with trend metrics that were not stored at the time.

historyRetention.reclaimableNote: {{reclaimable}} can be reclaimed from the database file. Physical compaction may wait until scans are idle.

playbackHistory.availabilityHelp: Jellyfin keeps individual playback starts in its activity log only for a limited history. MediaLyze can therefore separate playbacks only from the earliest event it has synchronized; older Jellyfin data remains an aggregate per-user value. The exact boundary is marked on the timeline.
playbackHistory.scopeNote: Individual playback starts imported from Jellyfin's retained activity log are shown on the timeline. Any difference from Jellyfin's per-user play count is preserved below without an individual timestamp. Event duration and completion are omitted because Jellyfin does not provide them for these activity entries.
playbackHistory.aggregateScopeNote: Jellyfin currently provides only the latest timestamp and an aggregate play count per user. The latest known playback is shown on the timeline and all remaining plays are preserved below without an individual timestamp.
playbackHistory.coverageSummary: Timestamped: {{timestamped}} of {{total}} · Without an individual timestamp: {{undated}}
playbackHistory.unknownTimeDescription: These plays come from Jellyfin's per-user total but cannot be assigned to an individual activity event. They remain visible regardless of the selected history range.
playbackHistory.noTimestampedPlaybacks: No individually timestamped playback is available. All known play counts are listed below.
playbackHistory.noTimestampedResults: No timestamped playback matches the selected range and filters.
playbackHistory.stackingTooltip: Unstacked shows every available playback start. Stacked combines adjacent events from the same user when their gap is shorter than one quarter of the asset runtime, or 10 minutes when no runtime is available.
playbackHistory.stackingUnavailableTooltip: Only one aggregate timestamp per user is currently available, so switching can leave the view unchanged. The control remains available and will apply automatically once individual playback events have been synchronized.
playbackHistory.showIndividualTooltip: Show each available playback event separately.
playbackHistory.groupNearbyTooltip: Combine adjacent playbacks by the same user only when their gap is shorter than one quarter of the asset runtime, or 10 minutes when runtime is unavailable.
playbackHistory.groupUnavailable: Individual event timestamps are required for grouping
playbackHistory.noResults: No playback data matches the selected range and filters.

transcoding.copyNote: Copied unchanged: codec, quality, language and stream metadata stay as in the source.
transcoding.actionHelp: Copy keeps the source stream unchanged. Encode converts it with the selected controls. Remove excludes it from the output.
transcoding.qualityHelp: Lower values mean higher quality and usually larger files. This encoder uses {{mode}} from {{min}} to {{max}}; the default is {{default}}. Typical guidance: {{guidance}}

qualityGuidance.globalQuality: For QSV ICQ, 18–28 is a useful starting range; VAAPI codec-native indexes vary, so start near the default and compare
qualityGuidance.default: start near the default and compare the result

transcoding.presetHelp: Faster presets reduce encoding time but usually reduce compression efficiency and increase file size. {{guidance}}

presetGuidance.x264: For H.264/H.265, medium is balanced; slow/slower favor compression and quality, while veryfast and faster favor throughput.
presetGuidance.qsv: For Intel QSV, medium is balanced; veryfast/faster favor throughput and slow/slower favor compression.
presetGuidance.nvenc: P1 is fastest; P4 is balanced; P7 favors quality and compression efficiency.
presetGuidance.amf: Speed is fastest, balanced is the default, and quality favors compression.
presetGuidance.svtav1: Lower SVT-AV1 numbers favor quality and compression but take longer; 6 is a balanced starting point.
presetGuidance.generic: Start with medium; choose a faster value for previews or a slower value for final storage.
presetGuidance.default: Start with the balanced value and compare speed, quality, and output size.

transcoding.resolutionHelp: Only equal or lower heights are offered. The width is calculated with even pixels so the source aspect ratio is preserved; upscaling is rejected.
transcoding.languageHelp: Values use BCP 47 formatting. ISO 639-1/639-2 aliases are normalized, regional subtags are retained, and unknown codes remain visible.
transcoding.bitrateHelp: Choose a standard target bitrate. Higher values preserve more audio detail and increase the output size. Lossless formats do not use a bitrate target.
transcoding.filenameTemplateHelp: The default template keeps the source name and appends the selected media metadata. Custom templates use tokens in curly braces and optional groups in square brackets.
transcoding.filenameTemplateOverrideHelp: When overriding, enter the metadata tokens and square-bracket groups you want to keep in the generated name.
transcoding.globalHistoryHint: Filter persisted jobs without deleting generated media files or variant links.
